_comment: Semester VI course packs — HAND-AUTHORED, like concepts.json/taxonomy.json. Each course: class metadata, a small concept graph (x,y hand-positioned for the constellation; keywords drive deterministic chunk/topic tagging), and a misconception taxonomy whose signals are phrased the way students write. Ids are namespaced per course so every table can hold all courses at once.

misconceptions.name: Believes the parser reads characters and makes the tokens itself
signals: parser splits the input into tokens
misconceptions.correction_hint: the lexer produces the token stream; the parser consumes tokens, never raw characters

misconceptions.name: Thinks an ambiguous grammar is only a performance problem
misconceptions.correction_hint: ambiguity yields multiple parse trees for one input — a meaning problem, not a speed problem

misconceptions.name: Treats inherited and synthesized attributes as interchangeable
signals: inherited attributes flow up the tree
misconceptions.correction_hint: synthesized attributes flow up from children; inherited attributes flow down or across from parent and siblings

misconceptions.name: Believes a listener can change the parse outcome while walking
signals: listener modifies the tree while walking
misconceptions.correction_hint: the walk happens after parsing is finished; a listener reacts to the completed tree

misconceptions.name: Believes a goroutine is an operating-system thread
misconceptions.correction_hint: goroutines are lightweight tasks scheduled by the Go runtime and multiplexed onto a few OS threads

misconceptions.name: Thinks eventual consistency promises convergence by a deadline
signals: eventual consistency has a time limit
misconceptions.correction_hint: eventual consistency promises convergence once updates stop, with no bound on when

misconceptions.name: Believes a broadcast is a loop of point-to-point sends from the root
signals: broadcast is just a loop of sends
root sends to each process in a loop
misconceptions.correction_hint: collectives are cooperative operations every rank calls; the library uses tree-structured communication, not a root-side loop

misconceptions.name: Believes Lamport timestamps give real wall-clock order
signals: lamport order is the actual order
logical clock tells which happened first in real time
misconceptions.correction_hint: logical clocks respect causality; concurrent events can be ordered either way and wall-clock time is not recovered

class.name: Foundations of Cyber Security — Semester VI
class.source: sem VI / Foundations of Cyber Security

misconceptions.name: Believes hashing is a form of encryption that can be reversed
misconceptions.correction_hint: a hash is one-way and keyless; encryption is reversible by whoever holds the key

misconceptions.name: Treats authentication and authorization as the same step
signals: login decides what you can access
misconceptions.correction_hint: authentication proves who you are; authorization decides what that identity may do — separate checks

misconceptions.name: Thinks a digital signature encrypts the message for secrecy
signals: signed so nobody can read it
misconceptions.correction_hint: a signature is a private-key operation over a hash: it proves origin and integrity, not secrecy

misconceptions.name: Uses virus and worm interchangeably
signals: worm is a type of virus
virus spreads by itself over the network
misconceptions.correction_hint: a worm self-propagates across the network; a virus needs a host file or user action to spread

misconceptions.name: Thinks MQTT is request-response like HTTP
signals: mqtt client asks the server for data
misconceptions.correction_hint: MQTT is publish-subscribe through a broker; clients publish to topics and subscribers receive without requesting

misconceptions.name: Believes the publisher must know its subscribers
signals: sender keeps a list of receivers
misconceptions.correction_hint: the broker decouples them: publishers know topics, never the consumers

misconceptions.name: Treats sensors and actuators as the same device class
signals: sensors and actuators are the same
actuator is a kind of sensor
misconceptions.correction_hint: sensors read the environment into data; actuators turn commands into physical action

misconceptions.name: Believes agile means no documentation
misconceptions.correction_hint: agile values working software over comprehensive documentation — it still writes the documentation that earns its keep

misconceptions.name: Thinks classic waterfall freely revisits earlier phases
signals: waterfall lets you redo the design later
misconceptions.correction_hint: classic waterfall is sequential with expensive backtracking; controlled iteration is exactly what the later models add

misconceptions.name: Classifies quality constraints as functional requirements
misconceptions.correction_hint: functional = what the system does; non-functional = qualities and constraints like performance, security, usability

misconceptions.name: Believes sprint scope can grow mid-sprint
signals: new tasks go into the running sprint
misconceptions.correction_hint: sprint scope is fixed at planning; new work goes to the product backlog for a later sprint
